title: Testing Web Applications
learning_outcomes: Explain what testing web applications contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: http-level tests.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Quality comes from several kinds of evidence: unit tests, integration tests, static analysis, coding standards, and repeatable CI. Tests should assert observable behavior and include important failure and boundary cases. In this lesson, focus on http-level tests; then compare it with routing tests. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use testing web applications when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Quality comes from several kinds of evidence: unit tests, integration tests, static analysis, coding standards, and repeatable CI. Tests should assert observable behavior and include important failure and boundary cases. For testing web applications, begin with http-level tests. Also distinguish routing tests; form validation tests; authentication and authorization tests. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: HTTP-level tests
items.text: Track where this value enters the request lifecycle and where it affects the response; client-provided data must be treated as untrusted.

items.title: Routing tests
items.text: Track where this value enters the request lifecycle and where it affects the response; client-provided data must be treated as untrusted.

items.title: Form validation tests
items.text: Write an assertion about observable behavior and include a boundary or failure case; a passing command alone does not prove the requirement.

items.title: Authentication and authorization tests
items.text: Distinguish identity verification from resource permission, and test expiry, invalid credentials, and denied access as well as the success path.

items.title: Response and cookie assertions

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Testing Web Applications
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$required = ["status", "message"]; $response = ["status" => 200, "message" => "ok"];
echo count(array_intersect($required, array_keys($response))) . " fields matched" . PHP_EOL;

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Test observable behavior, include boundary cases, and treat static analysis and coverage as evidence rather than proof.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for testing web applications from top to bottom. Start by identifying http-level tests, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of http-level tests.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary inputs and failures can reveal defects that normal examples miss.
common_mistakes.fix: Add empty, invalid, boundary, and failure cases with meaningful assertions.

common_mistakes.why: Tests can become brittle and stop checking real behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Prefer simple unit tests and focused integration tests at actual boundaries.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating coverage as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Executing a line does not guarantee its behavior was asserted.
common_mistakes.fix: Review assertions, relevant branches, edge cases, and regression risk.

summary: Testing Web Applications is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Test observable behavior, include boundary cases, and treat static analysis and coverage as evidence rather than proof.
